acceptanceCriteria.criterion: Given my financial data with a flexi facility, when I calculate the Hybrid Flexi-Snowball Strategy (FR19), then it combines flexi chunking methodology (use flexi for lump sums) with snowball target selection (smallest balance first).

Given my financial data with a flexi facility, when I calculate the Hybrid Flexi-Avalanche Strategy (FR20), then it combines flexi chunking methodology with avalanche target selection (highest rate first).

Both hybrid strategies park surplus in the flexi facility during the month, then chunk to the target debt account based on their respective targeting logic (snowball: smallest balance, avalanche: highest rate).
When the target debt account is paid off, both strategies roll the freed-up payment amount to the next account according to their targeting logic.
Both hybrid strategies have effort level = 'medium' (more complex than traditional methods, but simpler than velocity banking).
Given no flexi facility exists in the financial snapshot, when either hybrid strategy is calculated, then it returns null (not an error, just not applicable) with requiresFlexi = true.

Both strategies return a complete StrategyProjection with all required fields: strategyId, strategyName, effortLevel, debtFreeMonth, debtFreeDate, totalInterestPaid, totalPrincipalPaid, monthsSaved, interestSaved, monthlyProjections[].
Both strategies implement the DebtStrategy interface with calculate() and allocatePayment() methods, following the Strategy Pattern (ADR-004).
All calculations use big.js for precision with cent-level accuracy (2 decimal places in ZAR).
Unit tests verify that hybrid strategies correctly combine flexi chunking mechanics with their respective targeting methods.

Comparison tests verify hybrid strategies perform differently from pure flexi-chunking (which uses avalanche by default) and show expected behavior: hybrid-avalanche should save more interest, hybrid-snowball should have faster psychological "wins".

constraints.constraint: All monetary calculations must use big.js for precision. Never use JavaScript floats for financial math.
Follow Strategy Pattern - implement DebtStrategy interface with id, name, description, effortLevel, requiresFlexi, calculate(), allocatePayment().
Framework-agnostic - calculation engine code in src/lib/calculations/ must not import React or UI code.
Hybrid strategies have effortLevel = 'medium' (more complex than traditional, simpler than velocity banking).
Both hybrid strategies must return null when snapshot.flexiFacility is null (requiresFlexi = true).
Calculations accurate to 2 decimal places (cent-level ZAR). Rounding errors must not accumulate beyond 0.1% over 360-month projections.
All 8 strategies must calculate in under 3 seconds for typical portfolio (5-10 accounts).

interface.name: DebtStrategy
interface.signature: interface DebtStrategy { id: string; name: string; description: string; effortLevel: 'low' | 'medium' | 'high'; requiresFlexi: boolean; calculate(snapshot: FinancialSnapshot, config?: StrategyConfig, baseline?: StrategyProjection): StrategyProjection | null; allocatePayment(surplus: Big, accounts: SimulatedAccount[], flexi: SimulatedFlexi | null): PaymentAllocation[]; }

interface.name: StrategyProjection
interface.signature: interface StrategyProjection { strategyId: string; strategyName: string; effortLevel: EffortLevel; debtFreeMonth: number; debtFreeDate: string; totalInterestPaid: Big; totalPrincipalPaid: Big; monthsSaved: number; interestSaved: Big; monthlyProjections: MonthlyProjection[]; }

interface.name: PaymentAllocation
interface.signature: interface PaymentAllocation { accountId: number; amount: Big; }

interface.name: generateProjection
interface.signature: function generateProjection(snapshot: FinancialSnapshot, allocator: PaymentAllocator, config?: ProjectionConfig): MonthlyProjection[]

interface.name: buildStrategyProjection
interface.signature: function buildStrategyProjection(strategy: DebtStrategy, projections: MonthlyProjection[], startDate: string, baseline?: StrategyProjection): StrategyProjection
